auditor_value: (a) car frame: parabola in the floor plane, x_rel = −2.5t², z_rel = 10t, curving backward; (b) ground frame: straight line at a constant 10 m/s along k̂

findings.quote: Assuming the object also accelerates along k̂ in the ground frame gives a curved path in the ground frame, but the frictionless floor exerts no force there at all.
findings.note: An acceleration along k̂, the same line as the object's velocity, gives straight-line motion, not a curved path; the stated cause cannot produce the effect named. The real error is giving the object the car's acceleration along î in the ground frame.
findings.fix: Assuming the object shares the car's acceleration along î in the ground frame gives a curved (parabolic) path in the ground frame, but the frictionless floor exerts no horizontal force on the object at all.

notes: Answer agrees. Ground velocity at release is 10 k̂ because the car is at rest at that instant; all four equations check.
